intended_object: A universally catenary ring: a Noetherian commutative ring R such that every finitely generated R-algebra is catenary (Stacks 00NL). Taken from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The class asks for two things: `IsNoetherianRing R`, and that every finite-type R-algebra B is catenary. Here "catenary" is the library's `TauCeti.Excellence.IsCatenary B`, defined as `Order.IsCatenary (PrimeSpectrum B)`. That order-level notion requires two things for any pair of primes: strict chains between them have bounded length, and all saturated chains (chains of covering steps) with the same endpoints have the same length. This is exactly Stacks 00NI. Saturated chains between p and q are the same as maximal chains of primes from p to q, and for incomparable pairs both conditions hold vacuously.

The class only quantifies over algebras B in the universe of R. This loses nothing: every finite-type algebra is isomorphic to a quotient of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) R`, which lives in universe u. The library's documentation lists results that recover the statement in every universe (`isCatenary_of_finiteType`, `isCatenary_of_essFiniteType`).

The notion is stated for an arbitrary commutative ring, which is its natural generality. I found no Mathlib definition of catenary or universally catenary rings, so there is no counterpart to cite.
